what_happened: The command was RIGHT, but the ego drifted left across the yellow centre lines and drove in the oncoming lanes next to the parked cars on the far curb, about 10.6 m from the recorded path. Oncoming vehicle 85 closed fast (the gap fell from 24 m to 4 m in 0.5 s while the ego held about 8 m/s), and the ego hit it head-on/front-right without braking or steering back to its own side.

After handoff the policy steered left off its planned route on a narrow residential street, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Still speeding up to about 7 m/s, it drove into the row of parked cars on the left and hit parked car 15/31 head-on.

After taking over at 4.6 s, the policy did not follow its route, which stayed in the right travel lane. It drifted left out of the lane toward the left curb and the parked cars, speeding up from 8.5 to 9.4 m/s, and at 6.7 s it hit parked car 31 with its front, ending up off the drivable area.

With a RIGHT command at the intersection, the ego drifted left of its lanes and away from the recorded path (5 m off by 7.7 s, 12 m by 9.7 s). It kept heading toward the curb and the bollard-lined corner, slowing only to about 4 m/s, and drove off the drivable area at 9.7 s.

After handoff at 4.6 s, the ego was at the far left edge of a narrow residential street. Its plan ran straight up the parking lane next to the parked cars instead of moving right onto the recorded path. It sped up from 6.4 to 7.1 m/s without braking and hit parked car 15 head-on, about 1.2 m left of the recorded trajectory.

The route said turn RIGHT and the recorded human moved right, but after handoff the ego steered left across the double yellow centre line. It then drove straight in an oncoming lane and hit oncoming vehicle 85 head-on at about 9 m/s, with front contact about 9 m from the recorded path. This is wrong-way driving rather than a lead-vehicle or turning collision, and the camera view was clear beforehand.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path turned right, but the policy steered left of that path, toward the corner curb. It slowed from 7 to 4 m/s but kept going and drove over the curb onto the sidewalk past the bollards and tree, 12 m from the recorded path.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path moved right toward the turn. Instead, the policy planned and drove a path that drifted steadily left across the lanes and onto the landscaped median with palm trees, while slowing from 11.7 to 8.6 m/s. It went off-road at 9.0 s, 6.2 m from the recorded path, with no actor involved.

With a RIGHT command, the ego stayed on the wrong side of the double yellow centerline at about 9.8 m/s instead of following the human path to the right. It ended about 9.5 m off the recording and hit oncoming car 85 head-on, never slowing even though the car was clearly visible in its lane from about 8.4 s.

The ego was approaching the intersection at about 6 m/s, where the route turns right. Its own planned path (orange) pointed straight and then bent left across the intersection instead of following the right turn. Just after the stop line the ego angled slightly left and was flagged offroad, while still only about 0.5 m from where the human drove. No other actor was involved.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went right, but the policy kept drifting left at about 10–12 m/s. Approaching the intersection, it went over the left-side curb onto the median, toward a sign post, ending up 6.2 m from the recorded path. The camera was clean until the ego was already leaving the road, so the policy steered the wrong way on its own.

The command was RIGHT. The ego made a right turn at about 3.5–4 m/s, but it turned too tightly and cut toward the curb instead of following the human's path. It drove front-first into parked car 90 at the corner of the cross street, about 6.7 m off the recorded trajectory.

On the RIGHT command, the ego took the turn much too tight, cutting across the curb lane instead of following the planned path through the intersection. Its front hit parked car 90 at the curb at about 4 m/s, roughly 7 m off the recorded human path.

The policy took over at 4.6 s on a narrow street with cars parked on both sides. Instead of staying in the lane where the human drove, which was slightly to the right, it steered left toward the parked cars on the left curb. The route command was RIGHT. At 6.7 s, going about 7 m/s without braking, the ego's front hit the parked car ahead of it in that row (actor 31, possibly 15), about 1.2 m off the recorded path.

Despite a RIGHT route command, the ego drifted left away from the recorded path (about 9 m off by the end). It crossed the double-yellow centerline and drove in the opposing lanes at about 8–9 m/s, then hit oncoming vehicle 86 head-on. This was wrong-way driving into oncoming traffic; the later rear contact came after the front collision.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path ran up and to the right through the intersection. Instead, the ego kept going and drifted left of that path (about 4 m off by 7.5 s), with its planned path bending toward the left kerb. Still at about 4–6 m/s, it crossed onto the sidewalk/corner area near the tree and poles and was ruled offroad at 9.5 s, 12 m from the recorded trajectory.

The route command was RIGHT and the route turned right, but the ego stayed in a left lane and drifted further left as it approached the intersection. At about 9 s, at roughly 9 m/s, it ran onto the planted median, about 6.3 m from where the human drove. No actor was involved, and the camera view was clean until the ego was already on the median.

The route said RIGHT and the human turned right, but after handoff the ego stayed in its through lane at about 11–13 m/s. The white car ahead (actor 99) was almost stopped at the intersection, so the gap shrank by about 11–12 m/s. The ego slowed only slightly (13.3 to 9.3 m/s) and its front hit actor 99 at 8.7 s.

While making the commanded right turn into a narrow street lined with parked cars, the ego kept a path that hugged the left side instead of following the recorded path on the right. Its front clipped the parked black Audi (actor 68) at about 4 m/s, and it was still speeding up as the gap closed.

The ego was going straight at about 10 m/s toward a signalized intersection, well back from the lead car (27 m), when it was flagged offroad at 5.7 s, only 1 s after handoff. At that moment it was just 0.4 m from where the human drove, and the table shows zero collisions, so the flag looks like a map-boundary artifact at the stop line rather than a real drift or crash. The planned path heading straight/left while the route turns RIGHT is worth noting, but it had not caused the failure yet.

Although the command was RIGHT, the ego drifted left into the leftmost travel lane, about 10 m off the recorded path. There it closed on the slower vehicle 85 ahead (gap fell from 28 m to 2.9 m in 0.5 s) and hit it with its front while still going about 10 m/s, having slowed only slightly.

During a commanded right turn, the ego cut the corner far tighter than the recorded path (6.8 m off it) and drove front-first into parked car 90 at the curb, still speeding up to about 4.2 m/s. The camera view was clear while the turn was being set up; it only smeared at impact.

After crossing the intersection at about 4 m/s, the ego's planned path (orange) bent left, away from the recorded human path, which stays to the right. It drove into parked car 68 at the left curb without braking: the gap closed from 10 m to 4 m with speed holding at 4 m/s, and the front collision came at 8.8 s. The camera view was clean until the moment of impact.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path stayed in the right lanes, but the policy drifted left across its lane at about 10–11 m/s. By 8.8 s it had gone off the left edge of the road into the planted median and was heading into a palm tree, 6.2 m from the recorded path. No other actor was close; the at-fault collision flag is most likely the median or tree, since the actor collision metrics stay at 0.

The ego was approaching a signalized intersection at about 6 m/s, with no braking needed for the lead car about 30 m ahead. The route turns right (the command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT at 5.8 s), but the policy's planned path drifted left across the intersection toward the opposite lanes. The offroad flag fired at the stop line one second after handoff. The ego was only 0.4–0.56 m from the human's recorded track then, so the flag may be a marginal brush with the map's lane edge rather than a real departure, even though the plan was clearly wrong.

After handoff, the ego was driving straight at about 11 m/s with a lead car 16+ m ahead. Its planned path (orange) drifted left, away from the recorded path that kept right for an upcoming right turn. Entering the intersection, the ego's side hit actor 33, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded human path moved right across lanes. Instead, the policy kept planning a path that bent left. Starting at about 6.8s, the ego drifted left out of its lane and onto the planted median with the palm trees just before the intersection. It left the road at 8.8s, 6.2 m from the human path.

The ego was going straight through the intersection at about 10 m/s, with the route command switching to RIGHT. Instead of keeping its lane, the policy's planned path drifted left, about 1.5 m off the recorded human path, toward the adjacent lane. Its side hit actor 33, which was travelling alongside on the left. The camera view was clean before the impact, and the car ahead was never close (about 16 m).

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path stayed in the right lanes. Instead, the ego held about 7.4 m/s and steered left across the lanes into the tree-lined median on the left, where it went offroad at 9.6s, 6.4 m from the recorded path. The camera view was clean until the ego reached the median, and no actor was close by.
